$comment: THIS FILE IS THE SPECIFICATION for correction behaviour, not a test of it.
To change how corrections work: change a vector first, watch the test go red,
then make it green. Never adjust the corrector to satisfy a vector you did not
deliberately write, because that is how the documented behaviour and the real
Each case: entries (the dictionary), input (what the ASR produced), expected
(what must come out), and why (the rule being pinned).

cases.name: basic correction
cases.why: the simplest thing that must work
cases.input: let me open cloud code and check
cases.expected: let me open Claude Code and check

cases.name: case insensitive match, exact replacement casing
cases.why: the ASR varies capitalization freely; the dictionary decides the output
cases.input: Cloud Code and CLOUD CODE and cloud code
cases.expected: Claude Code and Claude Code and Claude Code

cases.name: RULE 2: whole matches only, no substring damage
cases.why: a rule for 'cloud' must never touch Cloudflare or cloudy
cases.input: Cloudflare fronts the cloudy cluster, but cloud is fine
cases.expected: Cloudflare fronts the cloudy cluster, but Claude is fine

cases.name: a broad trigger DOES damage legitimate standalone uses
cases.why: documents why the seed dictionary refuses 'cloud'->'Claude': whole-word matching cannot distinguish real 'cloud storage' from a misheard 'Claude', so a correction must be MORE specific than the word it replaces. This is desired behaviour, not a bug

cases.name: RULE 1: longest trigger wins
cases.why: 'claude code' must not be pre-empted by the shorter overlapping 'claude'

cases.name: RULE 3: glued and hyphenated words still match
cases.why: engines run words together; the gap is optional whitespace or hyphens
cases.expected: Claude Code, Claude Code, Claude Code, Claude Code

cases.name: RULE 5: a replacement is immune to later rules
cases.why: the sequential-replace bug: 'next js'->'Next.js' then 'js'->'JavaScript' would otherwise yield 'Next.JavaScript'

cases.name: RULE 4: NFC normalization
cases.why: a decomposed accented trigger silently never matches a composed one

cases.name: devanagari boundaries
cases.why: JS \b is ASCII-only, so Hindi triggers need unicode property boundaries

cases.name: disabled entries are inert
cases.why: turning a rule off in the UI must actually turn it off

cases.name: term entries never rewrite
cases.why: terms only bias the decoder; they are not corrections

cases.name: regex metacharacters in a trigger are literal
cases.why: a trigger is text the user typed, never a pattern

cases.name: empty and whitespace triggers are ignored
cases.why: a blank row in the editor must not match every position

cases.name: repeat count is tallied
cases.why: history shows whether an entry is earning its place

cases.name: applied records what the engine produced, not the trigger
cases.why: seeing the real error is what makes history useful for tuning

cases.name: no entries, text passes through untouched
cases.why: the empty dictionary must be a no-op, not a crash

cases.name: hinglish sentence with technical terms preserved
cases.why: the real workload: code-mixed speech where English terms must survive
cases.input: mujhe super base ka deployment cloud code se karna hai
cases.expected: mujhe Supabase ka deployment Claude Code se karna hai
